board.purpose: The one board sentence per page (h1). 2.75rem/42px phone, 4.75rem/84px from 720px, 5.25rem/84px from 1200px. Uppercase.

brand.purpose: Wordmark in the board's nav row.

stamp.purpose: Short uppercase statements on the ground and reading-page h2. 1.75rem phone, 2rem from 720px.

read.purpose: Paragraphs on About, Privacy and FAQ, max 65ch.

label.purpose: Form labels, legends, buttons, tabs, expander titles.

small.purpose: Hints, status, errors, nav links, footer.

motion.name: push-in
motion.value: 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), stagger 16ms per letter, from translateY(-0.32em) opacity 0.2
motion.purpose: Board letters dropping into the felt when the board's words change. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
Every page opens with a black felt letterboard in an oak frame. A few big, widely spaced capital letters on it say what is happening right now ("MAKE A CODE THAT NEVER EXPIRES", "THIS CODE CAN BE SWITCHED OFF"). The board is the page's status display, not a hero banner: when the job or the verdict changes, the board re-sets its words. Everything under the board is a quiet off-white working ground where the actual tool lives.

The system is flat and square. Areas are separated by 1px hairline seams, never by shadows, floating cards or rounded boxes. Colour is rationed: yellow means "the one thing to press", coloured letters on the board mean "this is the verdict", and everything else is ink on off-white. Density is low and text is short; the visitor is a non-technical shop owner who wants a working code in about ten seconds.

When you add a page (a dashboard, pricing, sign-in), start from the same skeleton: oak frame, board with the brand row and one short board sentence, then the working ground with seams. If the new page has nothing to say on the board, say what the page is ("Your codes", "Pricing", "Sign in"), in a few words.
keyCharacteristics: An oak-framed felt letterboard at the top of every page, carrying the brand, the nav and one short sentence.
Big Shoulders Display capitals on the board; Figtree for everything you read or type.
1px seams divide areas; no shadows, no cards.
One yellow primary action per screen.
Red, orange and green letters only for checker verdicts on the board.

rules.name: The One Yellow Rule
rules.body: Each screen has at most one yellow button, and it is the action the visitor came to do. Secondary actions are ink-outlined. If you are about to add a second yellow thing, one of them is not primary.

rules.name: The Verdict Letter Rule
rules.body: Red, orange and green letters appear only on the board, and only to state a checker verdict. They are never used for buttons, badges, charts, links or decoration. Ground-side messages use the darker `bad`, `warn` and `ok` instead, which pass contrast on off-white.

rules.name: The Only Pure Black Rule
rules.body: Pure #000000 belongs to the QR code itself. Interface "black" is felt/ink #1d1d1b.

rules.name: The Felt Groove Rule
rules.body: The felt has a 1px groove every 14px. Any line-height for text set on the board must be a multiple of 14px (the build uses 42px = 3 grooves on phones and 84px = 6 grooves from 720px) so letter rows sit in the grooves. If you introduce a new board size, pick its line-height from 28, 42, 56, 70, 84, 98...

rules.name: The One Size Per Role Rule
rules.body: Each text role has one size per breakpoint, set by a variable in `:root` (`--t-board`, `--t-stamp`, `--t-read`, `--t-big`, `--t-body`, `--t-label`, `--t-small`). Use the variable; don't invent an in-between size.

rules.name: The Display-Is-Caps Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders Display is only ever 800, uppercase and tracked. Never use it for body text, lowercase, or long sentences.

rules.name: The Hairline Seam Rule
rules.body: Areas are divided by a single 1px line in `seam` (#dcd8cf) on the ground, or `board-seam` (#3a3936) on the felt. Never use `box-shadow` for depth, never put content in a raised card, never use a background block to separate sections. If two areas need separating, draw a seam between them.

dos: Do start every new page with the oak frame, felt board, brand row and one short board sentence set in Big Shoulders Display caps.
Do use the CSS variables in `:root` of `src/style.css` for every colour and text size; add a new variable rather than a raw hex.
Do keep board line-heights at multiples of 14px (42px, 84px).
Do divide areas with a 1px `seam` line (#dcd8cf) and white space.
Do give each screen exactly one yellow (#f2c230) primary button; make every other button ink-outlined.
Do keep corners square (0px) and targets at least 48px tall.
Do change the board through `setBoard()` so the push-in and the screen-reader copy stay correct.
Do keep the 3px ink focus outline (yellow on the board).
donts: Don't use `box-shadow` for depth, floating cards, rounded boxes or grey panels.
Don't use red, orange or green letters anywhere except a checker verdict on the board.
Don't use yellow for highlights, badges, links, icons or a second button.
Don't use pure black (#000000) in the interface; it belongs to the QR code.
Don't put Big Shoulders Display in lowercase, in a lighter weight, or in paragraphs.
Don't add a centred hero, blue tabs, gradient buttons or stock illustrations.
Don't add animations beyond the push-in, and never one that ignores reduced motion.
Don't load fonts or scripts from a third-party server.
